questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 1 | CE Q57
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
Two reservoirs are connected by two parallel pipes of equal length and of diameters 20 cm and 10 cm, as shown in the figure (not drawn to scale). When the difference in the water levels of the reservoirs is 5 m, the ratio of discharge in the larger diameter pipe to the discharge in the smaller diameter pipe is _________. (round off to two decimal places)

(Consider only loss due to friction and neglect all other losses. Assume the friction factor to be the same for both the pipes)
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Flow Through Pipes

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Parallel pipes; \(L_1 = L_2 = L\); \(f_1 = f_2 = f\); \(H = 5\) m; \(d_1 = 20\) cm; \(d_2 = 10\) cm; minor losses neglected.
  • Aim: Find the discharge ratio \(Q_1 / Q_2\).

Core Concepts:

Darcy-Weisbach Equation (in terms of discharge):

\[h_f = \dfrac{8 f L Q^2}{\pi^2 g d^5}\]

Parallel Pipes Principle: Head losses are equal across both pipes: \(h_{f1} = h_{f2}\).

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Equate Head Losses:\[\dfrac{8fL Q_1^2}{\pi^2 g d_1^5} = \dfrac{8fL Q_2^2}{\pi^2 g d_2^5}\]
  2. Simplify (cancel \(8, f, L, \pi^2, g\)):
    \[\dfrac{Q_1^2}{d_1^5} = \dfrac{Q_2^2}{d_2^5} \implies \left(\dfrac{Q_1}{Q_2}\right)^2 = \left(\dfrac{d_1}{d_2}\right)^5\]\[\dfrac{Q_1}{Q_2} = \left(\dfrac{d_1}{d_2}\right)^{5/2}\]
  3. Calculate the ratio:\[\dfrac{Q_1}{Q_2} = \left(\dfrac{20}{10}\right)^{2.5} = (2)^{2.5} = 2^2 \times \sqrt{2} = 4 \times 1.4142 = 5.657\]

Note: The 5 m head difference is redundant data here, as it cancels out in the ratio.

Final Answer:

\[\boxed{\dfrac{Q_1}{Q_2} \approx 5.66}\] Accepted range: 5.60 to 5.70

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 1 | CE Q58
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
Depth of water flowing in a 3 m wide rectangular channel is 2 m. The channel carries a discharge of 12 m³/s. Take \(g = 9.8\) m/s².

The bed width (in m) at contraction, which just causes the critical flow, is ________ without changing the upstream water level. (round off to two decimal places)
questions.explanation:
Open Channel Flow | Specific Energy & Critical Flow

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data: Rectangular channel; upstream width \(B_1 = 3\) m; upstream depth \(y_1 = 2\) m; discharge \(Q = 12\) m³/s; \(g = 9.8\) m/s².
  • Aim: Find the contracted width \(B_2\) that just induces critical flow without altering the upstream pool level (choking threshold).

Core Concepts:

  • Specific Energy: \(E = y + \dfrac{V^2}{2g}\)
  • Choking Limit State: At the minimum contracted width, critical flow occurs exactly at the throat with \(E_2 = E_1\) (no upstream backwater).
  • Critical Flow in Rectangular Channel:\[E_c = \dfrac{3}{2}y_c \implies y_c = \dfrac{2}{3}E_c\]\[B_c = \sqrt{\dfrac{Q^2}{g \cdot y_c^3}}\]

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Upstream Velocity and Specific Energy:\[V_1 = \dfrac{Q}{B_1 y_1} = \dfrac{12}{3 \times 2} = 2 \text{ m/s}\]\[E_1 = 2 + \dfrac{2^2}{2 \times 9.8} = 2 + \dfrac{4}{19.6} = 2 + 0.2041 = 2.2041 \text{ m}\]
  2. Critical Depth at Contraction Threshold:\[E_c = E_1 = 2.2041 \text{ m}\]\[y_c = \dfrac{2}{3} \times 2.2041 = 1.4694 \text{ m}\]
  3. Solve for Minimum Contracted Width:\[B_2 = \sqrt{\dfrac{Q^2}{g \cdot y_c^3}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{144}{9.8 \times (1.4694)^3}}\]\[= \sqrt{\dfrac{144}{9.8 \times 3.1725}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{144}{31.090}} = \sqrt{4.632} = 2.152 \text{ m}\]

Final Answer:

\[\boxed{B_2 \approx 2.15 \text{ m}}\] Accepted range: 2.05 to 2.35

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 1 | CE Q59
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: A wastewater sample contains two nitrogen species, namely ammonia and nitrate. Consider the atomic weight of N, H, and O as 14 g/mol, 1 g/mol, and 16 g/mol, respectively. In this wastewater, the concentration of ammonia is 34 mg NH₃/liter and that of nitrate is 6.2 mg NO₃⁻/liter. The total nitrogen concentration in this wastewater is ________ milligram nitrogen per liter. (round off to one decimal place)
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Wastewater Characteristics

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension / Application
  • Given Data: Aqueous NH\(_3\) = 34 mg/L; Aqueous NO\(_3^-\) = 6.2 mg/L; Atomic weights: N = 14, H = 1, O = 16 g/mol.
  • Aim: Find the Total Nitrogen (TN) concentration in mg N/L.

Core Concepts:

  • Total Nitrogen (TN): Mass sum of elemental nitrogen in all nitrogen-containing compounds in the sample.
  • Nitrogen Mass Fraction:\[\text{Fraction of N} = \dfrac{\text{Atomic weight of N in molecule}}{\text{Molecular weight of compound}}\]

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Molecular Weights:\[MW_{\text{NH}_3} = 14 + (3 \times 1) = 17 \text{ g/mol}\]\[MW_{\text{NO}_3^-} = 14 + (3 \times 16) = 62 \text{ g/mol}\]
  2. Elemental Nitrogen from Ammonia:\[\text{N from NH}_3 = 34 \times \dfrac{14}{17} = 34 \times 0.8235 = 28.0 \text{ mg N/L}\]
  3. Elemental Nitrogen from Nitrate:\[\text{N from NO}_3^- = 6.2 \times \dfrac{14}{62} = 6.2 \times 0.2258 = 1.4 \text{ mg N/L}\]
  4. Total Nitrogen:\[TN = 28.0 + 1.4 = 29.4 \text{ mg N/L}\]

Final Answer:

\[\boxed{TN = 29.4 \text{ mg N/L}}\] Accepted range: 29.0 to 30.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 1 | CE Q60
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question:
A 2 % sewage sample (in distilled water) was incubated for 3 days at 27 °C temperature. After incubation, a dissolved oxygen depletion of 10 mg/L was recorded. The biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) rate constant at 27 °C was found to be 0.23 day⁻¹ (at base e).

The ultimate BOD (in mg/L) of the sewage will be___________. (round off to the nearest integer)
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Wastewater Engineering / BOD Kinetics

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Sewage sample concentration = 2%; incubation period \(t = 3\) days; temperature = 27°C; DO depletion = 10 mg/L; BOD rate constant \(k_{27} = 0.23\) day⁻¹ (base \(e\)).
  • Aim: Calculate the ultimate BOD (\(L_0\)) in mg/L.

Core Concepts:

  • Dilution Factor (DF): A 2% sewage sample means 2 parts sewage in 100 parts total.\[DF = \dfrac{100}{2} = 50\]
  • BOD Calculation: \(BOD_t = \text{DO Depletion} \times DF\)
  • First-Order BOD Kinetics:\[BOD_t = L_0\left(1 - e^{-k \cdot t}\right)\]

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate 3-day BOD of raw sewage:\[BOD_3 = 10 \text{ mg/L} \times 50 = 500 \text{ mg/L}\]
  2. Calculate Ultimate BOD (\(L_0\)):\[500 = L_0\left(1 - e^{-0.23 \times 3}\right) = L_0\left(1 - e^{-0.69}\right)\]\[500 = L_0(1 - 0.5016) = L_0 \times 0.4984\]\[L_0 = \dfrac{500}{0.4984} \approx 1003 \text{ mg/L}\]

Final Answer:

\[\boxed{L_0 \approx 1003 \text{ mg/L}}\] Accepted range: 1000 to 1005

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 1 | CE Q61
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question:
A water treatment plant has a sedimentation basin of depth 3 m, width 5 m, and length 40 m. The water inflow rate is 500 m³/h. The removal fraction of particles having a settling velocity of 1.0 m/h is ________. (round off to one decimal place)

(Consider the particle density as 2650 kg/m³ and liquid density as 991 kg/m³)
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Water Treatment / Sedimentation

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis / Comprehension
  • Given Data: Basin depth \(H = 3\) m; width \(B = 5\) m; length \(L = 40\) m; inflow \(Q = 500\) m³/h; settling velocity \(v_s = 1.0\) m/h. (Particle and liquid densities are distractors — \(v_s\) is already given.)
  • Aim: Calculate the removal fraction of the particles.

Core Concepts:

  • Surface Overflow Rate (SOR, \(V_0\)): The settling velocity of the design particle that is 100% removed. Depends only on plan area, not depth:\[V_0 = \dfrac{Q}{B \times L}\]
  • Removal Fraction (\(\eta\)): For an ideal rectangular basin:
    • If \(v_s \geq V_0\): \(\eta = 1\) (100% removal)
    • If \(v_s < V_0\): \(\eta = \dfrac{v_s}{V_0}\)

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Surface Area:\[A_s = B \times L = 5 \times 40 = 200 \text{ m}^2\]
  2. Surface Overflow Rate:\[V_0 = \dfrac{500}{200} = 2.5 \text{ m/h}\]
  3. Removal Fraction:
    Since \(v_s = 1.0 \text{ m/h} < V_0 = 2.5 \text{ m/h}\):\[\eta = \dfrac{v_s}{V_0} = \dfrac{1.0}{2.5} = 0.4\]

Final Answer:

\[\boxed{\eta = 0.4 \quad (40\% \text{ removal})}\] Accepted range: 0.38 to 0.42

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 1 | CE Q62
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question: A two-phase signalized intersection is designed with a cycle time of 100 s. The amber and red times for each phase are 4 s and 50 s, respectively. If the total lost time per phase due to start-up and clearance is 2 s, the effective green time of each phase is ______ s. (in integer)
questions.explanation:
Transportation Engineering | Traffic Engineering / Signal Design

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Number of phases \(n = 2\); cycle time \(C = 100\) s; amber time per phase \(A_i = 4\) s; red time per phase \(R_i = 50\) s; lost time per phase \(t_{Li} = 2\) s.
  • Aim: Find the effective green time \(g_i\) of each phase.

Core Concepts:

  • Cycle Length Components:\[C = G_i + A_i + R_i\]
  • Effective Green Time:\[g_i = G_i + A_i - t_{Li}\]
    (Actual green + amber, minus lost time due to start-up delays and clearance.)

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate actual green time (\(G_i\)):\[100 = G_i + 4 + 50 \implies G_i = 100 - 54 = 46 \text{ s}\]
  2. Calculate effective green time (\(g_i\)):\[g_i = G_i + A_i - t_{Li} = 46 + 4 - 2 = 48 \text{ s}\]

Alternative Verification: Total lost time \(L = 2 \times 2 = 4\) s. Total effective green \(= C - L = 100 - 4 = 96\) s. Since both phases are identical, \(g_1 = g_2 = 96/2 = 48\) s. ✓

Final Answer:

\[\boxed{g_i = 48 \text{ s}}\]

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 1 | CE Q63
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question: At a traffic intersection, cars and buses arrive randomly according to independent Poisson processes at an average rate of 4 vehicles per hour and 2 vehicles per hour, respectively. The probability of observing at least 2 vehicles in 30 minutes is _______. (round off to two decimal places)
questions.explanation:
Transportation Engineering | Traffic Engineering / Probability Models

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Car arrival rate \(\lambda_c = 4\) veh/h; bus arrival rate \(\lambda_b = 2\) veh/h; observation time \(t = 30\) min \(= 0.5\) h; independent Poisson processes.
  • Aim: Calculate \(P(X \geq 2)\) in 30 minutes.

Core Concepts:

  • Additive Property of Poisson: Sum of independent Poisson variables with parameters \(\lambda_1\) and \(\lambda_2\) is Poisson with \(\lambda = \lambda_1 + \lambda_2\).
  • Poisson PMF: \(P(X = k) = \dfrac{e^{-m} \cdot m^k}{k!}\) where \(m = \lambda \cdot t\).
  • Complementary Probability: \(P(X \geq 2) = 1 - [P(X=0) + P(X=1)]\)

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Combined arrival rate and mean:\[\lambda = 4 + 2 = 6 \text{ veh/h}, \qquad m = 6 \times 0.5 = 3 \text{ vehicles}\]
  2. Calculate individual probabilities:\[P(X=0) = \dfrac{e^{-3} \cdot 3^0}{0!} = e^{-3} \approx 0.04979\]\[P(X=1) = \dfrac{e^{-3} \cdot 3^1}{1!} = 3e^{-3} \approx 0.14936\]
  3. Calculate \(P(X \geq 2)\):\[P(X \geq 2) = 1 - (0.04979 + 0.14936) = 1 - 0.19915 = 0.80085 \approx 0.80\]

Final Answer:

\[\boxed{P(X \geq 2) \approx 0.80}\] Accepted range: 0.78 to 0.82

The peak hour factor (PHF) for 10 minute sub-interval is ___________. (round off to one decimal place)
questions.explanation:
Transportation Engineering | Traffic Engineering / Traffic Volume

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension / Application
  • Given Data: Traffic volumes in 10-minute intervals: 10, 11, 12, 15, 13, 11 vehicles.
  • Aim: Determine the Peak Hour Factor (PHF) for a 10-minute sub-interval.

Core Concepts:

Peak Hour Factor (PHF): Ratio of the total hourly volume to the peak sub-interval flow rate, scaled to an hourly rate:

\[PHF_n = \dfrac{V}{\dfrac{60}{n} \times V_{n(\max)}}\]

Where \(V\) = total hourly volume, \(n\) = sub-interval duration (min), \(V_{n(\max)}\) = maximum volume in any \(n\)-minute interval.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Total hourly volume:\[V = 10 + 11 + 12 + 15 + 13 + 11 = 72 \text{ vehicles/hour}\]
  2. Maximum 10-minute volume:\[V_{10(\max)} = 15 \text{ vehicles (30–40 min interval)}\]
  3. Calculate PHF:\[PHF_{10} = \dfrac{72}{\dfrac{60}{10} \times 15} = \dfrac{72}{6 \times 15} = \dfrac{72}{90} = 0.8\]

Final Answer:

\[\boxed{PHF = 0.8}\]

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 1 | CE Q65
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question:
For the dual-wheel carrying assembly shown in the figure, P is the load on each wheel, \(a\) is the radius of the contact area of the wheel, \(s\) is the spacing between the wheels, and \(d\) is the clear distance between the wheels. Assuming that the ground is an elastic, homogeneous, and isotropic half space, the ratio of Equivalent Single Wheel Load (ESWL) at depth \(z = d/2\) to the ESWL at depth \(z = 2s\) is _________. (round off to one decimal place)

(Consider the influence angle to be 45° for the linear dispersion of stress with depth)
questions.explanation:
Transportation Engineering | Pavement Design / ESWL

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Load on each wheel = \(P\); contact radius = \(a\); wheel spacing = \(s\); clear distance \(d = s - 2a\); depth \(z_1 = d/2\); depth \(z_2 = 2s\); dispersion angle = 45°.
  • Aim: Find the ratio \(\dfrac{ESWL_{d/2}}{ESWL_{2s}}\).

Core Concepts:

Equivalent Single Wheel Load (ESWL): A single wheel load producing the same stress at a given depth as the dual-wheel assembly.

  • At depth \(z \leq d/2\): Stress dispersion zones from the two wheels do not overlap. At 45° dispersion, the spread radius at depth \(z = d/2\) just reaches the adjacent wheel's zone. Each wheel acts independently:\[ESWL_{(z \leq d/2)} = P\]
  • At depth \(z \geq 2s\): Stress zones fully overlap; both wheels act as a single combined load:\[ESWL_{(z \geq 2s)} = 2P\]

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. ESWL at \(z = d/2\):
    At 45° dispersion, lateral spread at depth \(d/2\) equals \(d/2\). The two stress cones just meet — no overlap. Therefore:\[ESWL_{d/2} = P\]
  2. ESWL at \(z = 2s\):
    At this depth, complete overlap occurs (per IRC guidelines). Both wheels effectively act as one load:\[ESWL_{2s} = 2P\]
  3. Calculate the ratio:\[\text{Ratio} = \dfrac{ESWL_{d/2}}{ESWL_{2s}} = \dfrac{P}{2P} = 0.5\]

Final Answer:

\[\boxed{\dfrac{ESWL_{d/2}}{ESWL_{2s}} = 0.5}\]
